analysis.title: semis just broke out heres why the squeeze could get violent
key_insights: SOX is breaking through key short-term resistance and is trading in almost uncharted territory. The authors would not be surprised by talk of fresh all-time highs soon.
SOX is overbought but still far from the extreme overbought levels the index usually reaches once a full squeeze is under way.
SOX still lags the Taiwan equity market, which the authors treat as the lead indicator for semis.
JPM's memory work argues supply/demand tightness could last through 2028. Micron sees CY27 and CY28 becoming tighter than CY26.
Demand continues to outrun supply, cleanroom capacity is constrained and HBM demand is growing considerably faster than conventional server DRAM.

Semi data remains strong: Taiwan server ODM revenues +130% YoY, Aspeed +118% YoY, Korean DRAM exports +412% YoY to a record. DDR5 and DDR4 spot prices keep rising and trade well above contract prices.
GS says expectations for conventional memory and HBM pricing were largely washed out and are starting to recover, with more investors looking for upside to current pricing assumptions.
The authors see reset expectations, improving fundamentals and a technical breakout as a setup for a squeeze.
The authors find playing SOX upside through options structures interesting. Vol is not cheap, but options trades are more sensible than during the earlier mania.
